messages:
clare: Quick brag + confession — solved my woeful home Wi-Fi with a plant-stand elevation trick. Put router on a tall metal plant stand, moved antennas vertical, and throughput went from 12Mbps to 140Mbps. :herb: :rocket:

pete: plant stand wizardry. did you actually measure or are we in folk-tech territory? :laughing:

clare: measured. ran before/after `iperf3 -c 1.1.1.1 -t 10` and saw steady improvement. also moved it off the carpet so vents could breathe.

anu: brilliant. i use a powerline adapter (TP-Link) through the breaker for my desk. works most days but got weird latency spikes last week. anyone tried pairing powerline + plant-stand?

milo: powerline tip: avoid plugging adapters into surge-protected strips. plug straight into wall for best results.

ops-bot: ops-bot: ISP maintenance window reported 2026-12-19T09:00:00Z09:15:00Z for residential sector S4. Short jitter observed 09:05:1209:07:40 UTC. Please check local status pages.

zara: that might explain the little hiccup i saw. also clare, did you secure the router so Fluffy can't knock it over? :cat:

clare: yes, weighted the base with a small pouch of rice and zip-tied it lightly. Fluffy approved but attempted to chew the zip tie later. :sweat_smile: pic: http://imgur.com/placeholder_plantstand

pete: rice pouch genius. also note: if you're using powerline adapters on different phases in an older house, latency can spike. i had to move one to a wall on the same breaker to fix packet loss.

anu: thanks. how do you check phase issues without calling an electrician?

milo: pragmatic check: try swapping outlets or move the adapter to a different room on the same floor and see if latency changes. `ping 1.1.1.1 -c 20` and compare stddev. if it improves, likely phase/noise issue.

clare: added a short WFH networking checklist to #devex: "Elevate router, avoid strips for powerline, tether as contingency, label cables." happy to add pics and the quick iperf command.

ops-bot: ops-bot: Note added to INC-2026-879: residential jitter in S4; advise users to test wired fallback and report persistent issues to ISP.

zara: shoutout to @clare for the plant-stand idea. small changes, big wins. :tada:

pete: also remember ventilation: keep at least 4-6 inches clearance. overheating routers throttle.

anu: bookmarking the checklist. and bringing a sack of rice to my next plant-stand build. :grin:
